newsitem.title: USA: Cargill, N Korea continuing to work on grain deal.
newsitem.headline: Cargill, N Korea continuing to work on grain deal.

text.p: Officials from Cargill Inc are continuing to be in contact with North Korean officials to work out an agreement over the financing and other specifics of an approved 500,000-tonne grain shipment to the famine-stricken nation, a Cargill spokesperson said Thursday.
"We're continuing to negotiate, and that's the extent of what we're saying about the discussions," said Lori Johnson from Cargill's headquarters in Minneapolis.

Senior Cargill officials were in Pyongyang last week to work out an agreement and left over the weekend without a successful conclusion, but have remained in contact with North Korean officials since then.
Johnson said it is likely that Cargill representatives will be returning to North Korea, but said she was unaware if another round of face-to-face meetings has been scheduled.
Officials are trying to work out the financing of the deal, and what commodities will be shipped. Cargill received approval to ship 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice.

Speculation has been that Cargill was interested in a barter arrangement with North Korea, but Cargill officials have not confirmed those reports. Reports also circulated earlier this week that North Korea was asking the U.S. government to help finance the shipment, but those reports also remain unconfirmed.

Johnson repeated earlier statements that the Cargill negotiations are completely separate from an upcoming briefing with North Korea on proposed peace talks that is scheduled for Feb 5 in New York. North Korea earlier this week postponed the talks because it reportedly wanted to complete the negotiations with Cargill first.
Johnson said it is uncertain if a deal would be worked out by the scheduled start of the New York talks.
